evidence: snapshot-producer.lisp:1-2: "; The actual captured source portion of the online snapshot job." Line 19: :source (fnn-snapshot-source-begin captured). Also fnn-hsr-source-begin (125), fnn-hsr-cold-step (195), fnn-hpi-offer (288) and fnn-hpi-action (300). grep finds no (defun ...) for any of them under host/. fnn-owner-snapshot-capture, fnn-snapshot-job-source-step, -cleanup, -log-durable and -restart-source have no callers outside this file, and only the WIP snapshot-startup.lisp references the file. planning/ledger.json lists fnn-snapshot-source-begin as undefined, and HST-040 is 'planned'.
fix: Mark the file PARKED the way receiver-turn-parked.lisp is (state what is undefined and that no build loads it), or remove it until the HPI writer lands. When it is wired in, classify fnn-store-error refusals separately from :uncertain, and release the canonical and publication captures on the refusal path.
reviewer: snapshot-producer.lisp is referenced only by the comment at snapshot-startup.lisp:1 ('Production startup assembly WIP'). host/native/build.lisp does not load it (grep finds no other reference in host/tools/tests/books). fnn-snapshot-source-begin, fnn-hsr-source-begin, fnn-hsr-cold-step, fnn-hpi-offer and fnn-hpi-action have no defun under host/ or books/. The refuse-io at 129 is caught by the generic error arm at 437-439, which sets :uncertain. This is dead code with a misleading 'actual capture' header and has no runtime effect.
scenario: A reader or lane treats the job's refusal/uncertain bookkeeping as live code. It is not, and parts of it are already wrong. For example, fnn-refuse-io "snapshot source reader refused" (line 129) is caught by the generic error arm at line 439, which sets outcome :uncertain, so a definite pre-I/O refusal would force recovery. Anyone wiring the file in inherits that collapse and unreleased canonical/publication captures on the refusal path of fnn-owner-snapshot-capture (603-607 are acquired, but the cleanup at 624-631 releases only root, view and capture).
title: snapshot-producer.lisp is unloaded WIP that calls five undefined functions, but its header describes it as the actual capture
